correctness.rationale: For finite real B1B2=0, orthogonal singular pairs split the weighted Euler matrix into exact 2-by-2 blocks and scalar zero modes. An explicit computation of both singular values of [[a,-b],[-c,a]] gives norm sqrt(a²+(b-c)²/4)+(b+c)/2. Since it increases with singular value sigma, the attained top s mode controls the whole matrix. Convexity and exact squaring with strict boundary signs yield hcrit; differentiation gives unique hstar, and minimization of a one-dimensional convex expression in log(r) over the exact condition interval yields rK, CK and Kcrit. Real Dirac eigenvalues give separate sharp Schur interval. A seven-dimensional filled-triangle incidence witness confirms the strict Euclidean-versus-weighted distinction. Symbolic stationarity substitutions and the checker run directly from packaged material corroborate arithmetic; the infinite-parameter theorem is proved analytically.

value.rationale: An asymptotically stable explicit Euler discretization can amplify Euclidean errors at every positive step, whereas a fully symmetrizing metric may have a large condition number. The exact K-dependent minimal coupling C_K, critical budget, optimal step, and sqrt(K) transient prefactor give a mathematically natural implementation tradeoff. A concrete filled triangle needs K>256/9 but full symmetry requires K=256. The complete sharp classification handles all positive parameters, metric budgets, and equality cases rather than an arbitrary finite enumeration.
